# Kition kit rules (read first)

<!-- kition-quality:begin (generated by kition-sdk tools/sync-quality.mjs; edit the template there) -->
## Quality rules (read first)

- Tests are the spec. Read `docs/quality.md` and the feature catalogue (`features.yaml`)
  before changing behaviour. When code and a case disagree, the case wins unless a maintainer
  approves changing the case.
- Before you finish any task, run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`. If it fails, the task is not done. Claude Code
  runs it for you through the Stop hook; agents without hooks (Codex) run it by hand and
  report the real exit code.
- The full checks and tests run on GitHub, in the kit's CI run, not on your machine: a task is
  done only when HEAD has a passing CI run and is on `origin/main`. Use Kition's
  `scripts/kit-ci.sh` (`push`, `wait`, `failures`, `land`; Kition's `docs/kits.md`, section
  4c). Compile only the crates you touched locally.
- Never edit expected results to make a test pass: files under `cases/**/expected/`, paths
  listed under `protected` in `features.yaml`, and the `expected`, `tolerance`, `reference`,
  `input` and `steps` of an existing `case.yaml`. If you believe an expected result is wrong,
  stop and explain why in the task's findings; only a maintainer approves expected-result changes.
- Never weaken a test to make it pass: no deleted or loosened assertions, no added
  `#[ignore]`, `.skip`, `.only` or `.todo`, no raised tolerances. kition-sdk's
  `tools/check-expected.mjs` lists every such change for the maintainers.
- Every bug fix starts with a failing case under `cases/regressions/issue-<n>/`, then the fix.
- Every new feature adds an entry to `features.yaml` and at least one gating test.
- Put the task id and the case ids in the commit message.
- Stage only your own files: `git add` them by name; never `git commit -a` or `git add -A`.
  Other sessions may have uncommitted work in the same checkout.
- Commit on `main` in the repository's main checkout: no git worktrees, and one agent per
  repository at a time.
- Never start `cargo xtask eval` (the real-model `layer: eval` cases): only a maintainer starts it (F-QA-16). Write eval cases and check them with `--dry-run`, which calls no model.
- No compatibility layers: no aliases, old names, old file suffixes, migrations, or readers for
  old formats. Delete a replaced path in the same change.
<!-- kition-quality:end -->

This repository is Kition's `kit.board` kit. The engine is Kition's own, in Rust.

- Read Kition's `docs/kits.md` and this repository's `docs/design.md` before kit work. The
  Kit Harness Protocol (KHP) and the kit platform contracts live in kition-sdk and khp;
  change them there, never here.
- **The replica is the document; the file holds its content, not its history.** A `.kboard` file
  is a ZIP of the replica's content (`content.json`: its state, no deleted content, no version, no
  origins) and the blobs the state references (`docs/design.md` section 2, kition-sdk rule M16b). Never
  write `snapshot()`, a change log or anything a save changes (times, counters) into the file;
  the history is the host's.
- **Bound connector ends are derived** from the target's box and the stored anchor; the stored
  point is a cache for outside readers (`docs/design.md` 1.4). Never write a repair transaction for
  something a reader can derive.
- **Repairs are deterministic.** Every validation rule depends only on the state, never on arrival
  order or actor, and writes only when something is wrong (`docs/design.md` 1.5).
- **The editor draws nothing of its own.** Under R2c the page draws each element with the engine's
  SVG fragment and sends every change as one engine command at the end of a gesture; it never
  writes the page replica itself.
- `bindings/wasm` must keep passing `kition_kit::testing::check_contract`, and `kit.json` must
  pass kition-sdk's `tools/check-manifest.mjs` (`cargo xtask manifest`).
- The editor (`web/`) draws on `@kition/sdk/editor` with the host's theme tokens; files go only
  through the host. Never run the engine on the page's thread.
- Code, comments, docs, tests, fixtures, and commit messages are English. Commit messages name the
  task card id. No host paths, user names, or secrets in tracked files.
- Code moved or ported from Kition or another kit names its source in the commit message that
  brings it in; there is no change ledger.
- Two workflows, both calling Kition's reusable workflows: CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the
  kit CI) and Package (`.github/workflows/package.yml`, which publishes the kit's package). Do not
  add other workflows, and do not start the Package workflow: releasing is the owner's step.

## Never crash

- No panics in non-test code: no `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!`,
  `unimplemented!`, no slice indexing (`get()` instead); no `unsafe`. The workspace lints deny
  them; tests may use them (`.clippy.toml`). The one exception is a provably infallible literal,
  with `#[allow(clippy::expect_used)]` and a reason.
- Errors are `Result`s with typed reasons (`invalid-params`, `not-found`, `read-only`, ...).
  Input-derived numbers are hostile: finite checks, checked arithmetic.
- Every crash fix lands with a regression test.

## Working here

- On your machine, run only the fast checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p
  <touched crates> --all-targets`, the wasm check (`cargo xtask wasm`) and `pnpm typecheck` in
  `web/`. The full checks run in the kit's CI run on GitHub: clippy, `cargo test --workspace`,
  `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests including `check_contract`, wasm check) and
  every `test:*` script of `web/`. A task is done when the CI run of HEAD passes and HEAD is on
  `origin/main` (Kition's `scripts/kit-ci.sh` `push`, `wait`, `land`).
- Parallel agents: separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per agent.
